text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- British Foreign Office Minister Derek Fatchett says no change in Britain's policy towards Kuwait. Britain was a key player in U.S.-led coalition which drove Iraq's troops from Kuwait in 1991.
- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah receives message from Turkish President Demirel.
- Kuwait Hotels Company studying Syria, Lebanon and Egypt projects, Chairman Fawzi al-Qassar says.

- Social Affairs and Labour Minister Kulaib reaffirms Kuwait's eagerness to secure foreign workers' rights. More than half of Kuwait's two-million-strong population are guest workers mainly from Asian and other Arab countries.
- Parliament approves, in first of two votings, a bill to pay Kuwaiti pensioners a monthly allowance of 50 dinars ($166) for every child born to them after their retirement.
- Kuwait sends humaintarian aid to Bangladeshi cyclone vicitms.
- Dubai permits nationals of Gulf Cooperation Council countries -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates -- to buy apartments in the small emirate.
